specs.scene: An overhead flat-lay of a restaurant kitchen pass counter, dense with the establishment's own tools: blank order tickets clipped to a rail, a coiled thermal receipt roll, a stack of guest checks, a chef's pen, a small cash tray, a pair of tongs and a folded kitchen towel, crowded toward all four edges with two bare patches of stainless steel showing through, a line cook's hands entering from the bottom edge reaching for a ticket.
specs.source_quote: who notices eight thousand small software companies?

recognisable.why: a restaurant kitchen pass is an everyday, familiar working surface even without a brand.

legibility.why: the flat-lay is dense with several distinct objects a viewer must separately resolve, softened only by their gestalt as 'kitchen clutter.'

curiosity.why: 'invisible by design' implies a verdict about why this business escapes notice, without resolving it.

subject.why: hands anchor the frame but the true subject is diffused across many small objects rather than one mass.

credible.why: no figure is carried, which the rubric scores as full.

stakes.why: invisibility implies a mixed threat/protection to the viewer's own venture, though not sharply personal.

reexpress.why: the image supplies the consequence (invisibility) while the title supplies the smallness mechanism, without repeating it.

specs.scene: A documentary photograph of a small independent bakery counter: a glass pastry case, a stack of folded paper bags, a till drawer, and a jar of wooden stir sticks arranged plainly on the counter, the wall behind bare and blank, ample blank space above the counter for a caption.
specs.source_quote: What protects you is not their incomprehension. It is their indifference.

recognisable.why: a bakery counter is an instantly familiar everyday trade scene.

legibility.why: the counter reads as one coherent photographic mass, not a set of separate elements to decode.

curiosity.why: the caption states a flat, unresolved verdict the viewer cannot confirm by looking, the exact top-quartile pattern in this lane.

subject.why: the counter is a single working surface but has no single dominant object or person anchoring it.

credible.why: no figure is carried, scored full per rubric.

stakes.why: the verdict directly implicates the viewer's own business surviving on neglect rather than merit.

reexpress.why: the image carries the consequence (protection via indifference) while leaving mechanism and subject to the title.

specs.scene: A single countertop card payment terminal resting alone on a plain restaurant counter, its screen face blank and unlit, the surrounding counter otherwise bare.
specs.source_quote: six hundred seventy-five thousand dollars each

recognisable.why: a card payment terminal is a universally recognisable manufactured object, explicitly cited as an ideal example.

legibility.why: one object alone on a bare counter resolves as a single focal mass with nothing else to decode.

curiosity.why: a concrete stated figure closes the loop rather than leaving a verdict unresolved.

subject.why: the terminal is a single, distinctive object anchor with no ambiguity.

credible.why: the figure is quoted verbatim from the script in its smallest honest per-firm unit.

stakes.why: the number implies a realistic income ceiling relevant to the viewer's own venture, though it is descriptive rather than threatening.

reexpress.why: the figure reframes an aggregate industry number into a per-firm reality, though no title figure exists here to split against directly.

specs.scene: A barber mid-cut in a small barbershop, scissors raised close to a seated client's head, a bare wall left open to the left of frame, ordinary shop fixtures visible in soft background blur.
specs.source_quote: Software Is Going Where the Barber Went

recognisable.why: a barber cutting hair is one of the most universally recognisable trades and actions.

legibility.why: one person mid-action against a clean background is a single unambiguous focal mass.

curiosity.why: 'unbothered' implies a settled verdict about software's fate that invites but doesn't resolve the comparison.

subject.why: a person mid-action is the clearest possible human anchor.

credible.why: no figure is carried, scored full per rubric.

stakes.why: the destiny implied for 'software' extends to the viewer's own business trajectory, moderately personal.

reexpress.why: the image supplies the consequence (small, stable, unbothered) while the title supplies the mechanism and subject of the comparison.
